files.role: Public file-version request selectors, exact persisted identities, numeric/string codecs and local alias tests.
ranges: SPDX and Display/Formatter/FromStr, core DeepSizeOf/Error/Result and serde imports. Public canonical string constants are LEGACY_FORMAT_VERSION=0.1, V2_FORMAT_2_0=2.0, V2_FORMAT_2_1=2.1, V2_FORMAT_2_2=2.2 and V2_FORMAT_2_3=2.3. These string identities are distinct from footer numeric aliases.

Public const policy functions resolve stable_file_version to exact V2_2 and next_file_version to exact V2_3. This is the checked-out code policy, not external release verification or a complete list of format capabilities. No environment/configuration input changes these results.

LanceFileVersion is caller-facing Debug/Default/Clone/Copy/PartialEq/Eq enum: Legacy,V2_0,V2_1,Stable,V2_2,Next,V2_3. Default attribute is on exact V2_2, not Stable. Stable/Next are release selectors documented to resolve before dispatch and never enter persisted identities; this enum alone does not enforce all callers. No ordering or Hash derive.
DeepSizeOf for selector returns0 children because it owns no heap. Outer trait accounts inline enum storage.

resolve maps every exact selector directly, Legacy to V1 and policy selectors through stable/next helpers. is_unstable delegates to resolved ConcreteFileVersion. Both methods are const, consume Copy self and perform no IO or mutation.
Display writes canonical exact string for Legacy/V2 variants, but literal stable/next for policy selectors. It preserves selector intent rather than resolving it; formatter errors propagate.

FromStr lowercases the complete input without trimming. Accepts0.1 or legacy -> Legacy,2.0 or0.3 ->V2_0,2.1/2.2/2.3 exact, stable/next selectors. Other input returns unknown_version using original value. Thus mixed-case textual aliases work, whitespace and0.2 are not accepted; allocated lowercase String is transient.

Serialize uses Display text through serialize_str; Deserialize first requires a String then FromStr, mapping Error through serde custom. Selector serde can therefore retain stable/next and canonicalize legacy/0.3 aliases; it is not the strict manifest identity codec. Serializer/deserializer failures propagate.

ConcreteFileVersion is exact Debug/Clone/Copy/PartialEq/Eq/Hash enum V1,V2_0,V2_1,V2_2,V2_3. No Stable/Next, Default, ordering, serde or FromStr implementation is defined for this enum here. Documentation deliberately rejects ordering as a capability proxy. Hash derives enum identity, not a specified persisted wire encoding.

Concrete DeepSizeOf returns0 heap children. const to_selector maps V1 to Legacy and each V2 to its exact public variant, never Stable/Next. Converting resolve(Stable) back to_selector yields V2_2 and loses policy intent.

is_unstable is true only for V2_3. from_manifest_string matches canonical0.1/2.0/2.1/2.2/2.3 exactly, without case-fold/trim, rejecting caller aliases legacy,0.3,stable,next and all other strings. Error is InvalidInput via unknown_version, not CorruptFile.
to_manifest_string returns canonical static string for each exact enum. Paired with strict decoder it roundtrips exact identity, not original accepted numeric/footer spelling.

from_data_file_numbers accepts u32 pairs(0,0),(0,1),(0,2)->V1; (0,3) or(2,0)->V2_0; (2,1),(2,2),(2,3)->matching V2. Other pairs reject with formatted major.minor. Comments retain historical omitted/default metadata and v2.0 aliases; successful parse is identity recognition, not a per-file content/capability check.

to_data_file_numbers emits canonical u32 pairs: V1(0,2), V2_0(2,0), V2_1(2,1), V2_2(2,2), V2_3(2,3). Legacy numeric input aliases normalize when re-encoded. This is metadata encoding rather than standard v2.0 footer encoding.

from_footer_numbers accepts the same pair set as metadata parser but takes u16. V2.0 accepts standard writer(0,3) and embedded/self-described/mini writer(2,0) by documented roles. Rejects unsupported pairs with InvalidInput containing numeric text. No magic, length, page or encoding validation occurs here.

to_standard_footer_numbers emits u16 V1(0,2), V2_0(0,3), and remaining V2(2,minor). The v2.0 special case deliberately differs from canonical DataFile metadata. Actual writer invocation paths are not proven by this mapping alone.

to_embedded_footer_numbers emits u16 V1(0,2), V2_0(2,0), and V2_1/2/3(2,minor). Only V2_0 differs from standard footer function. No bytes/endian conversion happens until caller serializes these numbers.

Concrete Display delegates to to_manifest_string. Private unknown_version accepts impl Display and creates Error::invalid_input_source with Unknown Lance storage version: followed by value. It adds no reader path unless the supplied display value contains one.
cfg(test) imports FromStr,ObjectStore,Path,parent items and declares EXACT_VERSIONS array of all five exact variants. It drives codec test loops without claiming externally released fixtures.
selector_resolution_is_exact asserts all seven variant mappings and defaultV2_2. It pins current policy explicitly, not relative ordering or semantic capabilities.
public_selector_aliases_remain_unchanged asserts nine accepted strings including legacy and0.3 plus selectors. It does not test uppercase/whitespace/invalid input despite FromStr behavior.
Manifest codec fixture roundtrips all five exact identities and rejects legacy,0.3,stable,next via is_err only. No exact error variant/text assertions or corrupt file fixture here.
DataFile numeric fixture pins canonical output for five variants, decoder roundtrip, all three legacy(0,minor<=2) aliases and(0,3)->V2_0. No unknown/u32 boundary pair case.

Footer fixture separately asserts five standard and five embedded output pairs, decodes each, and accepts all legacy footer aliases. It verifies dual v2.0 representations locally without reading actual writer output or historical complete data files.

Async version-detection fixture writes8-byte synthetic footers to in-memory ObjectStore: little-endian major0, minors0..2, shared MAGIC, then calls determine_file_version with known size and expects V1. It checks recognizer acceptance only; those files have no pages/schema. Tests were inspected, not executed.

files.role: Crate module facade and asynchronous footer-only exact file-version recognition.
ranges: SPDX; public concat,datatypes,format,reader,testing,version,versions,writer modules; io is pub(crate), compatibility_tests private cfg(test). Public LanceEncodingsIo reexport exposes selected IO type despite module visibility. Reader/writer implementations are separate pending files.

Imports shared MAGIC, core errors, ObjectStore/Path and exact version. determine_file_version(store,path,known_size)->Result<ConcreteFileVersion> obtains size via await store.size only if unknown, checked-converts it to usize or InvalidInput with path. Supplied usize size is trusted without checking actual length; no explicit size lookup then. Underlying open behavior is delegated, so this does not prove all HEAD requests avoided.

Reject size<8 with InvalidInput source text and path, then await open_with_size and exactly requested range size-8..size. Compare footer[4..] to MAGIC; mismatch returns contextual InvalidInput. No explicit received-length check: fewer than4 returned bytes can panic on slice; other non8 lengths fail magic comparison. Store/range IO errors propagate. No full file parse or schema/page integrity check.

Decode first two little-endian u16 values from four bytes, then delegate ConcreteFileVersion::from_footer_numbers. Magic match implies exactly8 returned bytes for this equality check. Unknown version error lacks path because decoder formats just the pair. The helper recognizes accepted footer aliases only and cannot establish complete file validity.

files.role: Public metadata-only index-staleness selection by overlay version, field ancestry and fragment coverage.
ranges: SPDX and module rationale: overlay replacements leave preexisting index values stale, so affected rows should be excluded from index results and re-evaluated on a flat path. Imports HashMap,core Result/Schema,Roaring,DataOverlayFile,Fragment,IndexMetadata. This module calculates sets only; it neither executes a query nor loads values/index files.

overlay_exclusion_offsets accepts overlays, ordered field ID slice, index_version:u64 and schema, and creates empty RoaringBitmap. Each overlay with committed_version<=index_version is skipped, including equality; others are considered regardless of input sort order. Here index_version means dataset build version, not IndexMetadata.index_version algorithm revision.

For every file field position, compute overlay field ancestry and match any indexed ID by exact equality, indexed ancestor of overlay field, or overlay ancestor of indexed field. Only matching fields union coverage_for_field(position); errors propagate and the local partial bitmap is discarded. Sibling fields do not match via a shared ancestor. Exact IDs can match even if absent from schema; no explicit tombstone/negative-ID filter or physical/deletion bound. Schema ancestry is recalculated in inner comparisons and may allocate/walk repeatedly; source docs restricted-to-indexed-fields includes structural ancestors/descendants.

Private stale_offsets_for_fragment first checks all overlay versions<=build version and returns empty without field/bitmap work; empty overlay list passes all(). Otherwise delegates full overlay exclusion. This adds a version pass and does not rely on newest-last sorting.

Private covers_fragment treats None bitmap as covering any supplied u32 fragment ID; Some requires contains. Comment ties it to DatasetPreFilter legacy behavior, whose consumer implementation remains pending. This is conservative staleness masking for unknown index coverage, not changing metadata None to a stored full bitmap.

overlaid_fragments scans all input fragments, retains those with nonempty overlays and collects HashMap<u32,&Fragment> using f.id as u32. Cast truncates IDs above u32::MAX; duplicate/truncated IDs overwrite earlier entries. Map owns no fragments and performs no overlay validation. O(total input fragments) to build; O(overlaid fragments) is only the outer bound for subsequent loops, not total ancestry/bitmap work.

collect_overlay_stale_frags visits supplied map in unspecified HashMap order, skipping already stale IDs or uncovered fragments. For remaining entries compute offsets using full segment.fields and segment.dataset_version, and insert map key if nonempty. Covering dependency fields participate, not only keyed_fields. Existing entries are preserved. Any error can leave earlier inserts applied; no rollback. A caller-supplied map key is trusted independently of Fragment.id.

collect_overlay_stale_rows_for_segment applies same coverage/build-version/full-field logic and unions each nonempty offset result into stale.entry(map_key).or_default. It neither skips existing keys nor clears old bits and creates no new empty entry. On error earlier fragments remain changed but the failing fragment local result is not merged. No live-row/deletion filtering or value loading; scalar/vector usage in comments is caller intent until traced.

cfg(test) imports and bitmap helper plus flat schema fixture: five nullable Int32 fields named field_0..4, Arrow-to-Lance conversion then set_field_id(None). Test helpers use unwrap; no production schema mutation occurs.

nested_struct_schema builds outer.middle.{a,b} nullable Int32 hierarchy and assigns IDs; dense_overlay makes legacy DataFile metadata o.lance with supplied field IDs, dense bitmap and version. This fixture choice does not imply current overlay writers emit legacy files.
Version test at index dataset version5 excludes only overlay6 offsets[2,7], ignores overlay4[0,1] and equal-version5[9]. Asserts exact bitmap/empty result; no IO.
Field-aware test excludes nothing for unrelated field2 when querying3, and excludes[4] for dense fields[2,3]. It pins matching-field union despite other fields sharing the bitmap.

Nested-field test: overlay child a invalidates index on outer; does not invalidate sibling b; overlay middle invalidates index on a. These assert both ancestry directions plus sibling separation with exact offset sets.
Sparse test fields[2,4] have coverages[2,3] and[1]; querying4 returns[1], querying2 returns[2,3]. It confirms positional restriction, not mismatched-list validation.
Multiple newer overlays on field3 with[1] and[4,5] union to[1,4,5]. Does not test repeated cells with restoring values; exclusion conservatively unions writes without comparing values.

segment helper constructs IndexMetadata with supplied fields/dataset_version/optional fragment bitmap, empty covering, random UUID/name idx and default optional details/time/base/files. fragment_with_overlay makes Fragment::new(id) then appends one overlay. Neither helper simulates query/index creation.

Fragment collector test uses fragment3 with changed rows[1,2]: None coverage marks3 stale, Some([0]) yields empty and Some([3]) marks3. It tests unknown-versus-known coverage conservatism but only one fragment per call.

Row collector test likewise expects fragment3->[1,2] for None coverage and empty map when Some([0]) excludes it. Tests inspected only. No direct overlaid_fragments duplicate/truncation test, existing-output accumulation, multi-fragment partial-error, covering-field, deleted-row or tombstone fixture here.
files.limits: Every415 physical lines read. Public through format::overlay::staleness. Schema ancestry and coverage lookup already analyzed; query prefilter/flat fallback consumers, index freshness policy and transaction validation remain pending. No execution or guarantee of complete query correctness.

files.role: Data-file and fragment metadata, schema projection, deduplicated manifest conversion, lineage-carrier validation and protobuf/JSON boundaries. Public declarations are reexported by format; this is metadata logic, not a dataset reader or writer.
ranges: SPDX and dependencies: HashMap, NonZero, Arc; core Error/Result/DeepSizeOf/Schema; ConcreteFileVersion, CachedFileSize, object-store Path and serde; overlay sorting/tombstone, row-ID constants/metadata and row-version converters. Implementations of file-version parsing, cached size and overlay/version codecs lie outside this file.

DataFile derives Debug/Clone/PartialEq/Eq/DeepSizeOf with public path:String, fields/column_indices:Arc<[i32]>, major/minor:u32, CachedFileSize and optional base_id:u32. fields identify schema IDs; column_indices map corresponding positions, with -1 meaning no top-level column and extra unassociated columns allowed. Shared Arc arrays reduce duplicate owned lists; no size saving was measured. path is documented relative to dataset root, with base_id for external data.

Custom Serialize emits exactly seven named fields: path, fields, column_indices, file_major_version, file_minor_version, file_size_bytes, base_id. Arc arrays serialize as slices, making JSON arrays transparent; serializer errors propagate. It does not sort, validate or omit None base IDs.

Deserialize uses a local DataFileHelper: path/fields, Vec column_indices default empty, major/minor default zero, CachedFileSize and Option base_id. Moves vectors into new Arc slices, preserving other values. No validate/file_version call occurs, so serde decoding is not metadata validation or interning.

new takes explicit ConcreteFileVersion, converts it via to_data_file_numbers, moves path/vectors into String/Arc, wraps Option<NonZero<u64>> in CachedFileSize and preserves base_id. new_unstarted uses exact version but empty field/column lists, default size and no base. Neither constructor validates array lengths or field ordering.

Legacy constructors are frozen compatibility helpers: new_legacy_from_fields forwards supplied IDs unchanged with empty columns, V1 and unknown size; new_legacy obtains all schema IDs, sorts them (without deduplication), then forwards V1 plus supplied size/base. Their existence does not establish current writer usage.

schema nested project_field treats blob/packed struct as atomic: clone entire field only if its own ID is mapped. Otherwise recursively projects children; any surviving children retain a cloned parent even if parent ID is absent. A leaf survives only if mapped. With no surviving children, V2.0 alone retains a mapped structural parent with empty children, preserving its physical header. Comments explain evolved child IDs must not be substituted from current schema; actual null filling belongs to a reader outside this file.

V1-encoding metadata projects by IDs with include_all_children=false. Other encodings build HashMap from zipped fields/column_indices, keep only indices>=0, and recurse over full schema in its existing order, cloning schema metadata. Zip stops at the shorter list, duplicate IDs collapse in the map, negative columns are ignored and extra columns have no field mapping. Exact raw pairs (0,3) or (2,0) activate V2.0 structural-header retention; no full version validation is performed here.

Private uses_v1_data_file_encoding is exactly major==0 && minor<3; it is a local layout predicate, not the general version parser. Public file_version delegates both stored numbers to ConcreteFileVersion::from_data_file_numbers and propagates its errors. Exact mapping is now covered at rust/lance-file/src/version.rs:198-224.

validate checks only two shape rules. For V1 encoding, remove every TOMBSTONE_FIELD_ID then require strictly increasing live IDs (no duplicates); failure is CorruptFile at base_path.join(path) with unsorted/duplicate message. For other encodings require columns.len>=fields.len; extra columns accepted, failure contextual CorruptFile. It does not verify exact file version, nonnegative values, file existence, row count, base IDs or column uniqueness/range. V1 branch allocates a live-ID Vec.

DataFile to protobuf clones path and copies both Arc slices to Vec, preserves exact numbers/base, and writes cached size as value or zero. TryFrom protobuf moves path, creates fresh Arc slices, wraps raw size using CachedFileSize::new and always returns Ok; no validation. Size-zero interpretation belongs to CachedFileSize implementation, not an error here.

Default DataFileFieldInterner holds separate caches for field IDs and column indices plus one shared cache for inline created/updated version bytes. Private InternCache<T:Eq+Hash+Clone> is Small(Vec<Arc<[T]>>) or Large(HashMap<Arc<[T]>,()>), threshold16. Documentation claims multi-GB savings at20M fragments and a favorable linear-scan crossover for20-200-byte payloads; these are source assertions, not measured results.

InternCache starts Small(empty). Small scans for content equality and returns a cloned existing Arc; on miss converts Vec to Arc, inserts a clone, and promotes only when unique entries exceed16 (the17th miss). Promotion drains all stored Arcs into a HashMap. Large performs borrowed slice lookup, returning stored Arc or inserting new Arc. Caches grow without eviction; no interning across the two separate i32 caches. Lookup complexity is linear in unique entries and comparison length before promotion; map hashing/equality still depends on payload contents after it.

Private row-version converters receive generated oneof directly: inline Vec bytes pass through the shared u8 cache into RowDatasetVersionMeta::Inline; column marker becomes Column. Both functions return Result but known arms all succeed; no byte decoding or column validation. The shared cache can deduplicate equal created-at and last-updated-at byte payloads.

intern_data_file performs the same structural protobuf conversion as DataFile::try_from, but routes fields and column_indices through their respective caches. It preserves exact version numbers and base ID, wraps raw size and returns Ok without shape validation.

intern_fragment maps physical_rows>0 to Some(as usize), otherwise None; interns updated/created inline version bytes, then all base DataFiles. Overlay entries use DataOverlayFile::try_from and sort_overlays_newest_last, without this field interner. Deletion/row-ID metadata use optional TryFrom+transpose. Inline row IDs are not routed through inline_bytes. Conversion failures propagate after any earlier cache insertions, without rollback; it does not call carrier or DataFile validation.

DeletionFileType Array/Bitmap derives equality, serde and sizing; serde names lowercase array/bitmap, while suffix() returns arrow/bin respectively. DeletionFile contains read_version/id:u64, type, optional num_deleted_rows:usize and optional base_id:u32. Unknown deleted count is None; no path is constructed here.

DeletionFile protobuf conversion recognizes integer type0 Array and1 Bitmap, otherwise returns not_supported_source("Unknown deletion file type") without including the offending value. Deleted count zero maps None, positive casts to usize without checked conversion. Other fields move through; no count/file validation.

Fragment public fields: id:u64, base files Vec<DataFile>, overlays Vec<DataOverlayFile>, optional deletion/row-ID metadata, physical_rows:Option<usize>, optional updated/created row-version metadata. Docs define one fragment as different columns of the same rows and missing schema columns as null. Overlays have default empty serde and skip when empty; deletion/lineage options skip when None, while physical_rows remains serialized even when unknown. Overlay order is significant, later newer by contract; serde itself does not normalize it.

new(id) constructs empty base/overlay vectors and all optional metadata None. num_rows returns physical count if no deletion file, or physical minus known deleted count if both are known, otherwise None. Contrary to the nearby comment, the subtraction branch requires a known deleted count. Subtraction is unchecked and can underflow if metadata claims more deletions than rows; no Result is returned.

referenced_lance_files and mutable counterpart yield base DataFiles first then every overlay.data_file, without allocation/deduplication. Exhaustive destructuring intentionally forces future Fragment fields to be considered. They omit deletion files and lineage metadata objects; lineage columns residing in base files are included through those base files. The documentation still mentions external raw-byte lineage ranges, whereas current RowIdMeta variants are Inline/Column (rust/lance-table/src/format/row_ids.rs:141-156).

has_spilled_row_lineage is OR of RowIdMeta::Column and the two RowDatasetVersionMeta::Column states. row_lineage_file(field_id) scans only base files for fields.contains(id), returns None if absent, first file if unique, or CorruptFile naming the second carrier path and fragment/field IDs if duplicated across files. It accepts arbitrary i32 input and does not reject repeated IDs within one file or inspect column_indices/metadata state. Missing carrier is not itself an error in this lookup.

spilled_row_lineage_field_ids creates a Vec of reserved IDs in row-ID, created-at, last-updated-at order, including each only when its metadata is Column. It consults metadata, not schema/files; this is a retention requirement for consumers deciding which data files can be removed.

crate-visible validate_row_lineage_carriers loops the spilled IDs, propagates duplicate-carrier errors, returns Internal if a carrier is missing, delegates exact version decoding, and returns Internal when decoded V1 carries a spilled column. Non-V1 versions pass this check; absent spills pass vacuously. It reads metadata only, with no IO or column-index/page/count checks. Error messages include fragment/field and V1 path; it does not invoke feature-gate support.

from_json delegates serde_json::from_str with error conversion and no extra validation or overlay sorting. with_file_legacy creates one V1 DataFile using schema IDs, supplied physical_rows, empty overlays and absent deletion/lineage. It performs no IO.

with_file consumes/mutates self by appending DataFile::new with explicit IDs/columns/exact version/size and base_id=None; add_file does the same through &mut self. with_physical_rows sets Some, including zero. add_file_legacy appends schema-based V1 metadata with unknown size/base. None checks count consistency or writes files.

try_infer_version considers all referenced_lance_files across fragments, including overlays. If no referenced file exists, returns Ok(None). Otherwise parses first exact version, then parses every file (including first again) and rejects any unequal ConcreteFileVersion with InvalidInput naming both versions. It ignores manifest mixed-version capability bits and does no IO. This strict helper is used for missing-format inference, not proof all supported manifests must be homogeneous.

Noninterning Fragment::try_from follows the same physical zero->None and overlay conversion/sorting rules, uses DataFile::try_from for bases and RowDatasetVersionMeta::try_from for created/updated instead of shared version-byte cache. Row-ID and deletion optional conversions propagate errors. It neither validates field arrays nor checks lineage carriers, stable-row flags or schema consistency.

Fragment->protobuf maps deletion type enum, writes unknown deleted/physical counts as zero, clones inline RowIdMeta Bytes handle, emits empty RowLineageColumn marker for Column, delegates version oneofs, copies base and overlay vectors in current order. It does not sort overlays or validate; Some(0) counts lose their known-zero distinction on later decode. Other cloning/memory costs depend on nested converters.

cfg(test) imports Arrow schemas, legacy file constants, bitmap/JSON helpers. Dense overlay fixture carries offsets1/3, version7 and a legacy metadata DataFile; protobuf roundtrip checks complete Fragment equality and coverage_for_field at positions0 and5 returns same bitmap. It exercises metadata conversion, not on-disk legacy overlays.

Sparse overlay fixture with fields2/4 and coverage{2,3}/{1} roundtrips protobuf then asserts coverage by position0/1. No IO, null values, overlapping overlay resolution or feature-gate enforcement is exercised.

Out-of-order overlay versions5,2,2,3 roundtrip to2,2,3,5; field IDs2 then3 assert original relative order among equal-version overlays. This pins stable load ordering for ordinary Fragment conversion; interner sorting calls the same helper.

New legacy Fragment fixture builds nested struct(si:Int32,sb:Binary) plus Boolean schema, asserts fragment ID123 and single DataFile with sorted IDs0..3. It does not assert physical_rows or actual file data.

Fragment protobuf roundtrip uses Float16 schema and Array deletion descriptor with known count10, then repeats with no deletion. Equality asserts metadata preservation for these cases only; no row-ID, zero-count or error fixture.

Exact-version fixture checks no files->None, new/new_unstarted V2_0 persist(2,0), two V2_0 fragments infer V2_0, and V2_1 overlay/base mismatches error with2.0/2.1 context. Base mismatch also matches InvalidInput. No file bytes are generated.

Evolved-struct fixture changes current child ID while stale files keep old child: V2_0 projection preserves empty values parent plus id, V2_1 parent index-1 projection retains only id, and current V2_0 mapped child returns full schema. This tests projection metadata, not reader null materialization or blob/packed-struct branches.

JSON fixture pins path/field array/empty columns/legacy major-minor constants, null size/base, lowercase array deletion fields, physical_rows null and omission of empty overlays/None lineage. from_json roundtrip equals original. No malformed JSON or old release fixture is used.

Extra-column fixture constructs two fields and three column indices, using imported lance_file::format major/minor constants, and expects validate success. This test does not set an explicit nonlegacy ConcreteFileVersion, so the source here alone does not prove it reaches the non-V1 length branch. All tests in this file were read, not executed.

files.role: In-memory dataset manifest, metadata transformations, fragment accounting, protobuf conversion, writer/version descriptors and frozen V1 self-describing reader adapter. Selected public types/functions are reexported by format; ManifestSummary and VersionPart are public inside the private child but not reexported.
ranges: SPDX/imports connect async_trait, Bytes, chrono, DeepSizeOf, file schema adapters/exact versions and V1 dictionaries/reader, IO ProtoStruct/Reader/read_struct, Path, prost/Timestamp, maps/ranges/Arc, Fragment/interner/row IDs, feature bits, LanceCache/Schema/errors and ObjectStore/Registry. External IO/file parsing implementations remain pending.

Manifest derives Debug/Clone/PartialEq/DeepSizeOf. Public fields hold schema, dataset version/branch, optional writer version, Arc<Vec<Fragment>>, aux/index/transaction positions, u128 nanosecond timestamp, tag, reader/writer words, optional u32 max-fragment high-water mark, optional transaction path, next_row_id:u64, exact DataStorageFormat, config/table_metadata/base_paths maps. Only fragment_offsets:Vec<usize> is private. Docs require fragments sorted by ID with gaps, but constructors/conversion below do not sort or enforce this; public fragments replacement can stale the private offsets. Dataset version, writer-library version and data-file version are separate values.

DETACHED_VERSION_MASK is bit63 (0x8000000000000000); is_detached_version tests it only. compute_fragment_offsets maps each Fragment::num_rows().unwrap_or_default(), chains final zero, and scans prefix sums into N+1 entries, including terminal total (empty list->[0]). Unknown row count contributes zero; ordinary usize addition is unchecked. It preserves fragment order and performs no row-ID mapping.

Default ManifestSummary has seven u64 counters. Consuming conversion to BTreeMap<String,String> writes exactly total_fragments, total_data_files, total_files_size, total_deletion_files, total_data_file_rows, total_deletion_file_rows, total_rows, all decimal strings. Type is pub in private module, not facade-reexported, though callers can infer the summary return type and use its public fields.

Manifest::new accepts owned Schema, shared fragment Vec, storage format and base-path map; computes offsets, starts version1/current WriterVersion, zero timestamp/feature words/aux position/next row ID, absent branch/tag/index/transaction/high-water mark, and empty config/table metadata. It does not inspect formats, assign fragment IDs, validate schema/carriers or perform IO.

new_from_previous uses supplied schema/fragments and recomputed offsets; increments previous version with unchecked +1, retains branch/high-water/next row ID/storage/config/table metadata/bases and refreshes writer version. It clears aux/index/time/tag/transaction references and preserves only STICKY_PAIRED_FLAGS separately in reader/writer words. It neither normalizes nor validates half-set pairs and does not preserve covered-index bit here. Caller must restore index metadata as comment states.

shallow_clone is in-memory: clones each Fragment, stamps ref_base_id only on base and overlay DataFiles whose base_id is None via referenced_lance_files_mut, and similarly stamps local deletion descriptor. Existing external base IDs remain. Inline/column metadata remains cloned; no files are opened/copied.

Shallow clone keeps source version/writer/aux position/time/high-water/offsets/next row ID/storage/config/table metadata, uses new branch and transaction_file=Some(input), clears tag/index/transaction_section, and allocates a new fragment Arc. It masks each feature word to covered-index bit OR sticky pairs, preserving each side independently. Source comments justify conservative covered-index retention; index metadata copy happens outside this function. Base map is cloned and insert(ref_base_id, BasePath(...,is_dataset_root=true)) can replace an existing entry without collision validation.

timestamp splits u128 nanos into remainder<1e9 and casts whole seconds to i64, uses chrono from_timestamp with unwrap_or_default fallback for unrepresentable date, then Utc. No error returned. set_timestamp actually accepts u128 raw nanos despite DateTime doc wording. config_mut/table_metadata_mut/schema_metadata_mut return mutable maps with no validation, persistence or feature recomputation.

field_metadata_mut delegates recursive schema field_by_id_mut then yields metadata or None. Deprecated update_config extends config with key overwrite semantics; deprecated delete_config_keys retains entries whose names are absent from supplied slice. No table configuration semantics are checked.

Deprecated replace_schema_metadata replaces whole schema map. Deprecated replace_field_metadata replaces selected field map and returns Ok, or InvalidInput with field ID if missing. The preceding no-op comment is inconsistent with the implemented error branch; document the error as behavior. No primary-key validation is invoked.

detach_sparse_inline_row_ids sums visible lengths of Inline row-ID payloads (not deduplicated, not created/updated versions). Returns unchanged if sum==0 or sum.saturating_mul(4)>=buffer_len, preserving exact quarter boundary. Otherwise Arc::make_mut obtains fragments and each Inline gets Bytes::copy_from_slice wrapped in a fresh InlineRowIds (new digest memo); other metadata unchanged. A shared fragments Arc triggers clone-on-write. Caller-provided buffer_len is trusted; whole original buffer release is not guaranteed while other owners/slices survive. Ordinary sum can overflow; multiplication is saturating.

update_max_fragment_id returns for empty fragments, otherwise takes maximum u64 ID then try_into u32 and unwraps (panic above u32::MAX). It initializes absent mark or raises it only, retaining historic high water after deletes. No Result or ID validation; a stored larger mark is preserved.

max_fragment_id returns stored u32 mark widened to u64 if present, otherwise computes maximum existing fragment ID, with None only for unset+empty. max_field_id compares schema max (default-1) with every field ID in base and overlay referenced files (default-1); includes dropped schema fields and does not explicitly filter tombstone or reserved IDs. No field IDs are assigned.

fragments_since rejects since.version>=self.version, including equality, with InvalidInput describing newer version. It uses since.max_fragment_id as threshold and clones current fragments with strictly greater IDs, or all if absent. This is an ID-high-water heuristic, not content comparison; docs exclude recycling and it does not validate common lineage/branch.

fragments_by_offset_range uses logical row offsets, not row IDs: binary_search start in cached N+1 prefix offsets, otherwise insertion index minus1, then walk fragment indices. Break when fragment start>=end OR fragment end<=start; append(start,&Fragment) otherwise. Unknown current length acts as zero. It does not validate/recompute offsets, sort, deduplicate equal offsets or explicitly validate empty/reversed ranges. Duplicated offsets/zero-length fragments may select a zero-length entry and break before later data; callers need valid coherent counts. Returned elements borrow fragments, despite doc return wording showing owned Fragment.

uses_stable_row_ids checks reader word FLAG_STABLE_ROW_IDS only, not per-fragment metadata or writer word. serialized builds pb::Manifest then encode_to_vec: raw protobuf bytes suitable for IPC/temp storage, not a complete on-disk manifest with footer/sections/dictionaries.

summary folds fragments: total_data_files counts base f.files only and total_files_size sums only known sizes of those base files, excluding overlays/deletion/index files despite broad docs. total_rows sums only known f.num_rows; deletion_file presence counts even if deleted count unknown, known deletion counts sum separately. total_fragments is Vec length; total_data_file_rows=total_rows+total_deletion_file_rows, not sum of all physical counts when some lengths unknown. Ordinary u64 additions are unchecked; no IO resolves missing sizes/counts.

Async populate_manifest_schema_dictionaries is a V1 compatibility adapter. Exact V1 delegates populate_schema_dictionaries(&mut schema,reader).await; V2_0/V2_1/V2_2/V2_3 are explicit no-ops. No version selector or writer-library comparison is used. Included doctest wraps an async Result function, not ignore; it was not compiled.

BasePath stores public id:u32, optional name, is_dataset_root:bool and full URI/path String. new assigns without URI/ID validation; extract_path synchronously delegates ObjectStore::extract_path_from_uri(registry,&path), propagating Result. Actual parsing/registry behavior is pending; no store initialization in this body.

BasePath custom DeepSizeOf children adds name children + twice path children + size_of<bool>(). This literally overcounts path allocation relative to normal one-string ownership and adds inline bool as a child; source gives no rationale. It is an estimator, not measured retained heap.

WriterVersion stores public library/version Strings plus optional prerelease/build metadata. DataStorageFormat stores public file_format:String and ConcreteFileVersion; new uses literal lance, getter returns exact enum, Default uses stable_file_version() resolved elsewhere. TryFrom protobuf preserves file_format without checking it equals lance and parses version via from_manifest_string. Exact mappings are now covered at rust/lance-file/src/version.rs:19-27 and rust/lance-file/src/version.rs:172-261; selector acceptance remains distinct from persisted strings.

ManifestBuildConfig is a data-only public Debug/Clone struct with auto_set_feature_flags, resolved timestamp_nanos, use_stable_row_ids, optional legacy mode/storage_format, disable_transaction_file, migration_next_row_id and Arc<SpilledRowLineage>. Docs specify sticky row IDs, overwrite-only storage override precedence, migration bypass and prefetched spilled sequences needed for rewrite/update; no enforcement/default implementation occurs in this file. Clock resolution deliberately belongs to caller; cfg(test) clock mocking in lance is a source comment, consumer implementation pending.

VersionPart Major/Minor/Patch is pub in private module with no facade reexport. Private bump_version increments chosen semver u64 component, resets lower components for major/minor, leaves prerelease/build intact and uses ordinary unchecked additions.

Private split_version parses semver, returns None on error, extracts nonempty pre/build as optional Strings, clears both in parsed object and returns clean major.minor.patch plus separate components. Docs include rc/build/invalid examples. No library check here.

Deprecated semver is a distinct lenient parser: split self.version at first dash, parse first three dot-separated components as u32 with missing minor/patch default0, return remainder after dash as optional borrowed tag. Extra dot parts are ignored, explicit prerelease/build fields and library are ignored; plus-build in patch can cause parse failure. It is not equivalent to full semver::Version parsing despite doc wording.

lance_lib_version rejects library != exact lowercase lance, parses self.version with semver, then when separate prerelease/build fields are Some parses and overwrites corresponding parsed components. None leaves components embedded in version string intact. Any parse error returns None. Arbitrary nonsemver WriterVersion values remain constructible; only this interpretation fails.

Deprecated semver_or_panic wraps old parser and panics with raw version on failure. older_than uses lance_lib_version().expect then compares against release major/minor/patch with empty pre/build, so prerelease ordering follows semver. Deprecated bump expects valid Lance version, increments numeric part, clears only prerelease if keep_tag=false (build retained), splits back to clean fields and clones library. Non-Lance/invalid versions panic; future-private wording is intent, not current restriction.

WriterVersion Default outside cfg(test) parses compile-time CARGO_PKG_VERSION and emits library lance, clean version and separate pre/build, panicking if invalid. Under this crate cfg(test), same fields then bump(Patch,true), retaining pre/build but using next patch. Dependency builds do not automatically inherit cfg(test); no actual Cargo version value is asserted here.

ProtoStruct maps Manifest::Proto=pb::Manifest. BasePath From conversions copy/move matching id/name/root/path fields, no URI/duplicate validation. Converting owned BasePath to protobuf consumes Strings.

Manifest TryFrom starts timestamp conversion by casting signed seconds/nanos to u128 then sec*1e9+nanos; absent timestamp defaults later to0. Negative or out-of-range values are not validated and casts/arithmetic can wrap/panic according to overflow policy. Any Some writer_version message becomes Some even with empty library/version; the fully-set comment does not enforce nonempty fields.

A fresh DataFileFieldInterner converts all protobuf fragments, sharing repeated base field/column lists and inline version bytes across this manifest, preserving fragment order. It computes logical offsets and wraps fields/schema metadata. If reader stable-row bit is set but any fragment lacks row_id_meta, returns Internal All fragments must have row ids; empty fragment set passes. It does not decode inline sequences or validate Column carriers.

If data_format absent, infer exact version from all base/overlay files, rejecting mixed versions; with no files use stable_file_version when deprecated writer bit2 set, else V1. If data_format present, trust converted DataStorageFormat without comparing per-file versions. Then convert schema via FieldsWithMeta. This conversion alone does not invoke ensure_can_read_manifest/paired flag checks or reject fragment_tree.

Final Manifest retains raw version/branch/flags/high-water/next row/config/table metadata, casts aux/index/transaction offsets to usize without checked conversion, normalizes empty tag/transaction_file to None, and collects base-path entries by id into HashMap (later duplicate ID replaces earlier). Uses converted fragments/schema/format and computed offsets. Unknown/ignored protobuf fields including fragment_tree have no Rust representation here.

Manifest->protobuf omits timestamp if nanos==0, else divides into seconds cast i64 and subsecond i32 without overflow validation. Converts schema through FieldsWithMeta and separately encodes schema metadata String values as UTF8 Vec; clones branch/writer strings including separate pre/build and converts fragments in order. This conversion does not validate inputs.

Output sets fragment_tree=None, preserves metadata/flags/high-water/counts, casts usize positions to u64, writes absent tag/transaction file as empty String, always includes data_format with exact to_manifest_string, clones config and emits base_paths from HashMap values in unspecified order. transaction_section presence retained. This is a protobuf object conversion, not atomic manifest publication or canonical byte ordering.

Public async_trait SelfDescribingFileReader offers default try_new_self_described(ObjectStore,Path,optional&LanceCache): await store.open, convert reader into Arc then delegate required try_new_self_described_from_reader. Both require Self:Sized; from_reader accepts Arc<dyn Reader>. Docs prefer fragment readers for cached schemas; no caching algorithm or format detection is implemented by the trait default.

Only implementation here is V1FileReader: read_metadata(reader,cache), require metadata.manifest_position or Internal with reader path, read_struct<Manifest> at position, hydrate V1 dictionaries, take schema/max_field_id(default0), then call V1 try_new_from_reader with path, reader clone, Some(metadata), schema, numeric0,0,max ID and cache. Errors propagate at awaits; compatibility adapter does not add a V2 self-describing implementation. Meaning of delegated numeric arguments and file IO remain pending.

cfg(test) imports feature bit, overlay/data/deletion types, Arrow/core fields and bitmap. Shallow clone fixture with one base and one overlay asserts both local base IDs become7. It does not assert existing external IDs, deletion stamping, feature retention, URI behavior or disk clone.

Old empty manifest fixture with absent data_format recovers V1 without deprecated writer bit, current stable with it. Persistence rejection loops stable,next,legacy,0.3 and asserts conversion error. These are constructed protobuf values, not released historical fixtures or proof all version aliases are covered.

Canonical output fixture asserts V2_0 serializes version string2.0. Missing-format fixture recovers exact V2_0 from a file even when prior in-memory storage field was V1, then rejects V2_0/V2_1 files when protobuf format is removed. Explicit-format mixed-version validation is not tested here.

Detach fixture holds two10-byte slices of one64-byte buffer, supplies logical buffer_len80 then81. Exact quarter retains original pointers; below quarter copies both pointers outside original allocation and verifies second payload contents. It trusts the provided length, does not assert deallocation/RSS, Arc sharing or digest behavior.

Writer default fixture asserts lance, three-part clean version, cargo prerelease tag, no build metadata for this package, reconstructed Cargo major/minor and patch+1 under cfg(test), and each numeric bump produces greater version. expected_tag is split from Cargo text; fixture assumes package metadata layout, not a general parser proof.
Split-version test covers release, rc.1, rc.1+build.123, build-only and invalid string, with exact clean/pre/build components. Does not cover the deprecated lenient parser.

Writer tests compare rc.1<release, reconstruct rc.1+build.123 and all numeric/pre/build fields, and allow nonsemver WriterVersion custom-build-v1 while lance_lib_version returns None. No other-library or invalid separate-component fixture.
Deprecated older_than fixture requires rc2.0.0 below2.0.0/2.0.1 but not1.9.9, release2.0.0 not older than itself but older than2.0.1. Panic behavior for invalid/non-Lance input is not tested.

Offset-range fixture has three fragments of10/15/20 rows, expects0..10 first only,5..15 first two,15..50 latter two at offsets10/25;45..100 and200..400 empty. It does not cover zero/unknown counts, reversed/empty interior ranges or stale offsets.

Max-field fixture uses schema IDs0/2, multiple files/fragments including dropped ID43 and expects43. Tests dropped physical IDs beyond schema maximum without reading data or assigning IDs through Manifest.
Overlay max-field fixture puts ID43 only in overlay over base0 and expects43, proving referenced overlay IDs participate in high-water calculation. No tombstone/reserved-ID boundary case.

Config fixture constructs three-fragment manifest, extends config_mut with two keys and removes one; equality confirms in-memory map mutation. It does not recompute feature flags, persist metadata or test deprecated APIs.

Summary test starts empty manifest (all seven zero), two known-zero fragments (two files/fragments but zero rows/sizes), then three in-memory fragments100/250/75 (425 rows, three files, unknown sizes contribute0). Comments saying write files do not correspond to IO in this test.

Summary deletion fixture sets one known1000-byte file/50 physical rows/10 deleted, expects40 live,50 total-data rows,10 deleted and one deletion/file/fragment, then seven string-map entries. Overlay omission and unknown physical/deleted-count combinations are not tested. All file tests/doctest were read, not executed.
files.limits: All1825 lines read in bounded chunks. Visibility facade: rust/lance-table/src/format.rs:21-25. Local metadata conversion, counters and helpers are covered; transaction builder enforcement, commit flags/support checks, IO framing, exact file-version implementation, overlay rules, row-version codecs and dataset consumers remain pending. No build/test/benchmark, file-format release qualification or external-dependency behavior verification was performed.

files.role: Physical cell coverage metadata, stable overlay order, tombstoning and Roaring serialization boundaries.
ranges: SPDX and module contract: coverage uses physical offsets including deleted rows, never live-row numbering; values align to bitmap rank (number of set bits below the offset), one value column per field, no offset-key column. Shared coverage is dense, per-field coverage sparse. Parsed bitmaps are Arc-shared. Highest committed version wins; equal versions use later list position. Replacing base fields must tombstone stale slots without shifting per-field coverage. These are format invariants described here; actual rank-based reading/writing and commit retry stamping are outside this module.

Exports child staleness module (now analyzed at rust/lance-table/src/format/overlay/staleness.rs:1-415), imports core errors/deepsize, Roaring/serde, Path, DataFile and protobuf. Public TOMBSTONE_FIELD_ID:i32=-2 marks obsolete field slots. Negative IDs other than-2 are not implicitly tombstones in the helper below.

OverlayCoverage derives clone/equality and custom serde through private OverlayCoverageBytes. Shared contains Arc<RoaringBitmap> for all fields; PerField contains Vec<Arc<RoaringBitmap>> position-aligned with data_file.fields by contract. Types themselves impose no length/cardinality/physical-row bound. Clones share bitmap contents but clone the Vec of handles.

Private serialized enum has Shared(Vec<u8>) and PerField(Vec<Vec<u8>>), preserving Roaring bytes. deserialize_roaring maps Roaring decode error to CorruptFile with supplied path and original error text. There is no explicit exhaustion check for trailing bytes. Serde uses an empty path because owner context is unavailable.

serialize_roaring clones and optimize()s a bitmap, preallocates serialized_size bytes and unwraps Vec serialization; unexpected error would panic. From<OverlayCoverage> consumes Arc handles/Vec and serializes each bitmap via this helper without mutating shared originals. No cross-field equality deduplication in output.

TryFrom serialized coverage uses Path::default, deserializes every bitmap into a new Arc, and propagates first error. Empty per-field Vec is accepted. It cannot check alignment with data_file.fields because coverage is decoded in isolation.

DeepSizeOf deduplicates each Arc bitmap by pointer in shared Context. First visit adds size_of<RoaringBitmap> plus serialized_size proxy; later visits add0. PerField also adds Vec capacity times Arc handle size. Refcount allocation overhead is excluded and closeness of serialized-size proxy is a source comment, not measured memory. Distinct cloned Vec allocations are still charged separately.
dense wraps supplied owned bitmap in one Arc; sparse maps each supplied owned bitmap into its own Arc. Neither checks field count, offset range, overlap or rank cardinality.

DataOverlayFile exposes data_file, coverage and committed_version:u64, with Debug/Clone/equality/serde/DeepSizeOf derives. Version is documented as commit-time stamp restamped on retry; this struct has no commit or stamp routine and accepts arbitrary versions.

coverage_for_field returns an Arc clone. Shared returns its bitmap for any requested usize without checking field bounds. PerField gets only its bitmap Vec index and returns InvalidInput with bitmap count/requested position if absent. It does not compare data_file.fields length or reject tombstoned fields.
sort_overlays_newest_last uses stable slice.sort_by_key on committed_version ascending, preserving original order for ties. It mutates ordering only; no versions, fields or coverage change.

verify_overlays_newest_last scans adjacent windows and returns InvalidInput on first strictly descending version pair with both values. Empty/singleton/equal versions pass. This validates order only, not coverage/field shape or commit ownership; callers must invoke it to obtain write-side protection.

tombstone_overlay_fields rebuilds every overlay field list, replacing nonnegative IDs whose u32 value occurs in supplied fields with-2. Coverage and column indices are left in place, preserving position. It then retains overlays with any field !=-2, so empty field lists/all-2 overlays are removed and other negative IDs remain. Even untouched overlays get a fresh field Arc/list; supplied-field membership is linear for every field. It does not delete physical files, recompute sizes or validate schema.

From<&DataOverlayFile> always emits Some(data_file) and Some(coverage), selecting SharedOffsetBitmap or FieldCoverage with optimized serialized bitmaps, preserving version. DataFile conversion is delegated. No physical write, sorting, tombstoning or alignment validation.

TryFrom protobuf first requires data_file (InvalidInput), derives its path, then requires coverage (InvalidInput) and parses Roaring with that path (CorruptFile). Converts DataFile only after coverage parsing, preserves committed_version, and accepts empty/mismatched per-field bitmap counts. No validate/sort/version support check runs here.

cfg(test) missing-field fixture constructs no-coverage and no-data-file protobufs and asserts diagnostic substrings. It tests required option presence but not corrupted bitmap bytes or shape/cardinality errors.

Run-optimization fixture encodes dense offsets0..1_000_000, asserts <1% of prior serialized size and recovered coverage equality. It uses a legacy DataFile metadata constructor without writing a legacy file. Not executed.

Serde JSON roundtrip loops dense populated/empty, sparse populated+empty and zero-bitmap sparse coverage, asserting exact equality. These cases confirm intended empty representations, not field-count validation or persisted historical fixtures.

Tombstone fixture has sparse[3,5], single[5], untouched[7]; replacing5 leaves two overlays, first fields[3,-2] and last[7]. It does not assert coverage/column arrays or physically remove files; implementation leaves those arrays untouched.
Ordering test accepts empty and versions[1,2,2,5], rejects[2,1] with newest-last diagnostic. Stable tie sorting itself is covered in fragment tests, not here.
Sparse coverage lookup fixture accepts positions0/1 and rejects5 with field-position diagnostic. No Shared out-of-range or mismatch-length fixture. All tests read, not run.
files.limits: Every475 lines read. Module invariants are distinguished from enforcement. Reader rank merge, staleness implementation, transaction stamps and file IO remain pending; no runtime qualification.
